name: export-related-document-attachment
summary: Request Processor stage that fetches every regex-matched document relation and uploads each related document to an external API via multipart.

relation_pattern.description: regex over document-relation keys selecting what to upload, e.g. ^attachment_email_attachments_\d{8,10}(?:_\d+)?$

auth_ref.description: OAuth token endpoint URL (client_credentials), shared with the export's other stages for token-cache reuse

upload_url.description: attachment-upload endpoint, typically templated with the created resource id

file_field.description: multipart form-field name the target API expects for the file part, e.g. attachment[file]

status_field.description: schema field (ui type data, must pre-exist) receiving the upload HTTP status per iteration

provenance: Designed from the Coupa upload stage in export-pipeline-reference (paused 2026-06, finished 2026-07-03); cross-checked against two production Workday AP attachment paths — both embed attachments base64 inside the SOAP payload instead (see export-workday-soap-attachment-data), so this REST/multipart counterpart is NOT yet live-validated.
notes: Only the FIRST document in each relation's documents[] is fetched — one upload per relation, by engine design. Very large attachments risk serverless memory/timeout limits (the content is held in-memory per iteration; no verified hard cap — the old ~50 MB folklore is unconfirmed) — test the real size profile and filter oversize relations upstream. get_content yields a single object (not a 1-item list) when exactly one relation matches; verify iterate_over handles that shape before promoting. Repeated response-handler writes to the same status field during iteration auto-collect into a list. The status field must already exist in the schema (ui_configuration.type data) or the whole export fails with the generic exception blocker. Generating the relations/artifacts themselves (email-attachment relations, rendered payload documents) is out of scope. CANDIDATE: not live-validated on a REST target yet.
